The area of the triangle $△ABC$ is $4\,\text{mm}^{2}.$ Use $\sin30^{\circ}=\frac{1}{2}.$ Then, $AC=${{field-1}} $\text{mm}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}bc\operatorname{sin}⁡A,
$$

where $∠A$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =AB=2\text{ mm} \\ b & =AC \\ m∠A & ={30}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}=\frac{1}{2},
$$

we can calculate $b=AC,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ 4 & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 2\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘} \\ 4 & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 2\cdot (\frac{1}{2}) \\ 4 & =\frac{1}{2}b \\ b & =\frac{4}{\frac{1}{2}} \\ b & =8\text{ mm}.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that $AC=8\,\text{mm}.$
